questions.question: Which of the following bodies looked after the various aspects of the Competition Act 2002?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Competition Commission of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Competition Commission of India (CCI)** is a statutory body responsible for enforcing the Competition Act, 2002, in India.
 
• It was established on **14 October 2003**, and became fully functional in **May 2009**.
 
• The main objective of the CCI is to **prevent anti-competitive practices, promote competition, and protect consumer interests**.
 
• The CCI also ensures that mergers, acquisitions, and combinations do not have an adverse effect on competition in India.
 
• It comprises a **Chairperson and six members** appointed by the Central Government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Competition Act, 2002**

 
 
• It replaced the **Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act, 1969** to modernize competition law in India.
 
• The Act aims to **prohibit anti-competitive agreements, abuse of dominant position, and regulate combinations** (mergers and acquisitions).
 
• It ensures a level playing field for businesses and promotes consumer welfare.
 
 
 
• **Functions of the CCI**
 
 
• Conducting inquiries into anti-competitive practices.
 
• Imposing penalties on entities for violations of competition law.
 
• Advising the government on policies that may affect competition.
 
• Spreading awareness about competition and consumer rights.
 
 
 
• **Structure of the CCI**
 
 
• The CCI is headed by a Chairperson along with six members appointed by the government.
 
• It functions as a quasi-judicial body with the authority to pass orders, impose fines, and recommend corrective measures.
 
 
 
• **Key Cases Handled by the CCI**
 
 
• CCI has investigated and penalized many major corporations for cartelization, abuse of dominance, and unfair trade practices.
 
• Notable cases include action against DLF (real estate), Google (search bias), and cement companies (cartelization).

questions.question: In Kabaddi, how many players per team are allowed on the field of play at any one time?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**7**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **In Kabaddi, each team is allowed to have 7 players on the field of play at any one time.**
 
• The game is played between two teams, and each team can have a maximum of 12 players in their squad, out of which 7 are active on the field, and the rest are substitutes.
 
• The objective of the game is for a "raider" to tag as many defenders as possible and return to their half without being tackled.
 
• Kabaddi is a contact sport that originated in ancient India and is now a popular competitive sport worldwide, particularly in South Asia.
 
• The match duration is divided into two halves of 20 minutes each, with a 5-minute halftime break.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kabaddi Terminology:**

 
 
• **Raider:** The player who enters the opponent's half to tag defenders and score points.
 
• **Defender:** The players who try to stop the raider from returning to their own half.
 
• **Bonus Line:** A line in the opponent's half that gives the raider an extra point if crossed without being tackled.
 
 
 
• **Pro Kabaddi League (PKL):**
 
 
• India hosts the Pro Kabaddi League (PKL), a professional league founded in 2014, which has significantly increased the sport's popularity.
 
• PKL follows a franchise-based model similar to IPL (Indian Premier League) in cricket.
 
 
 
• **International Kabaddi:**
 
 
• Kabaddi is recognized by the International Kabaddi Federation (IKF) and is played in over 65 countries.
 
• It is also an official sport in the Asian Games, where countries like India, Iran, and South Korea dominate.
 
 
 
• **Types of Kabaddi:**
 
 
• **Standard Style:** Played on a rectangular court with 7 players per team.
 
• **Circle Style:** Played on a circular field, popular in Punjab and other rural areas of India.
